I've been farming these 6 mu in Dongfu village, Quzhou County, for over 40 years. My father farmed this land before me, and I know every corner of it. I'm 64 now, and my back isn't what it used to be, so I need a system that doesn't kill me with labor. That's why I'm sticking with what works — winter wheat followed by summer maize on all six mu. It's the same double-cropping system my neighbors use, and it gives me two harvests a year. I can't afford to gamble with new crops at my age.

For the wheat, I'll rotary-till the fields in late September and sow an improved variety, Jimai 22, around October 10th. The extension technician told me 15 kg of nitrogen per mu is the recommendation, but honestly, last year I put down about 18 kg and the wheat stayed greener through jointing. Better to waste a few yuan on extra fertilizer than risk a bad harvest. I'll spread about 50 kg of compound fertilizer per mu as basal dressing, then topdress with urea when the wheat turns green in spring. I'll irrigate three times: the winter irrigation before the ground freezes, one at jointing, and one at heading. For spraying, I'll do herbicide once and insecticide twice — three trips total.

After harvesting the wheat in early June, the window is tight, maybe five or six days. I don't have time to plough, so I'll plant hybrid maize — Denghai 605, same as my nephew uses — directly into the wheat stubble with no-tillage. I'll put compound fertilizer in the seed furrow at planting, about 40 kg per mu. Summer rain usually helps, but if it gets dry I'll irrigate twice. Two pesticide sprays for the maize should be enough: herbicide right after sowing, and insecticide later if I see corn borers.

I expect about 520 kg per mu from the wheat and 580 kg per mu from the maize. That's roughly what I've been getting the past few years, and I'm not looking to break records — I just want a stable year.
